title: Romance
tagline: From The Wedding Singer to Sunrise without noticing the water got hot.

levels.name: Popcorn
levels.note: A wedding singer, Rodeo Drive, the bleachers, one day on repeat, the Empire State, Harry and Sally, and four weddings.

levels.name: Modern favourites
levels.note: Cher, Darcy, erased memories, pudding, Vienna, Verona Beach and an iceberg.

levels.name: Golden age
levels.note: A Vespa, Paris, a hitchhike, a society wedding, Rick's and a railway café.

levels.name: Bittersweet
levels.note: Annie, Maude, Austen, Sirk and a lie.

levels.name: Heartbreak
levels.note: Brokeback, Carol and Wong Kar-wai's corridors.

levels.name: Final boss
levels.note: A barge in 1934 and a silent sunrise.

core.b: Adam Sandler's jilted 1985 wedding singer and Drew Barrymore's waitress. Every 80s song, a rapping granny, and Billy Idol on the plane. Dumb, happy, perfect.

br.note: Reese Witherspoon goes to Harvard Law. 'What, like it's hard?'

core.b: Julia Roberts's Hollywood Boulevard sex worker and Richard Gere's corporate raider. The shopping scene. A fairy tale and knows it.

br.note: Hugh Grant's bookshop and Julia Roberts's film star
Meeting the boyfriend's very rich family in Singapore

core.b: The Taming of the Shrew in a Seattle high school: Julia Stiles, and Heath Ledger singing on the bleachers.

br.note: Freddie Prinze Jr.'s Pygmalion bet. The staircase
Emma Stone fakes a reputation, The Scarlet Letter as running joke

core.b: Bill Murray relives one day until he becomes someone Andie MacDowell could love. Core on Fantasy.

br.note: Ryan Gosling teaches Steve Carell to dress

core.b: A widower's son phones a radio show, and Meg Ryan falls for Tom Hanks's voice. They barely meet until the Empire State Building.

br.note: Hanks and Ryan again, falling in love by email
Lubitsch's original pen-pal romance
Cary Grant, Deborah Kerr and the Empire State

core.b: Can men and women be friends? Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan argue about it for twelve years. 'I'll have what she's having.'
Hugh Grant stammers through four weddings and a funeral chasing Andie MacDowell. The funeral is the best bit. On the BFI list.

br.note: Big knickers, Hugh Grant versus Colin Firth in the street

core.b: Cher's Brooklyn widow falls for her fiancé's angry one-handed brother (Nicolas Cage). 'Snap out of it!'
Keira Knightley's Elizabeth and Matthew Macfadyen's Darcy, misty fields and the hand flex.

br.note: Emma in Beverly Hills. As if! Also on Comedy
Anya Taylor-Joy's Emma

core.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
core.b: Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet erase each other, and he changes his mind halfway through. Core on Drama.

br.note: Joaquin Phoenix falls for his operating system
Clooney and J.Lo in a car boot. Core on Crime & Noir

core.b: Paul Thomas Anderson: Adam Sandler's furious, lonely novelty-plunger salesman finds love, pudding air miles and a harmonium.

br.note: A mute cleaner and a fish-man. Also on Fantasy
A dressmaker and a poisonous love. Day-Lewis's last

core.b: Linklater: Ethan Hawke and Julie Delpy meet on a train and walk around Vienna all night talking. Nothing happens; everything happens.

seq.note: Nine years later, Paris, in real time

br.note: Two childhood sweethearts, 24 years later
Emma Stone and Ryan Gosling choose their dreams. Core on Musicals

core.b: Baz Luhrmann's Verona Beach: Shakespeare's words with guns called swords, Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes meeting through a fish tank, and Radiohead at the end. Also on Musicals.
Jack, Rose and the iceberg. Core on Epic.
Audrey Hepburn's runaway princess and Gregory Peck's reporter on a Vespa round Rome. Her debut, and an Oscar.

br.note: Wilder: Audrey between Holden and Bogart
Moon River; Mickey Rooney's yellowface has not aged

core.b: Cary Grant and Audrey Hepburn in Paris: everyone's lying, the romance is the point. Also on Comedy and Thriller.
Clark Gable and Claudette Colbert on the road: the hitchhiking leg, the Walls of Jericho. Swept the Oscars.
Katharine Hepburn's society wedding, with Cary Grant as the ex and James Stewart as the reporter. Champagne and wit.
Rick's Café, 'As Time Goes By', Bogart, Bergman and the Nazis closing in. The perfect Hollywood film.
David Lean: two married strangers meet at a railway station café and fall in love over Rachmaninov. Very British, devastating. BFI No. 2.

br.note: Max Ophüls' lifelong unrequited love. On Scorsese's list

core.b: Woody Allen and Diane Keaton fall in and out of love in New York. Core on Comedy.
A death-obsessed rich boy of 20 falls for a free-spirited woman of 79. Cat Stevens songs. On AFI's romantic comedy top 10.
Ang Lee and Emma Thompson's Austen: two sisters, Hugh Grant, Alan Rickman, Kate Winslet in the rain.

br.note: Merchant Ivory: Florence, Surrey and Daniel Day-Lewis as the prig. On the BFI list

core.b: Douglas Sirk: a widow (Jane Wyman) falls for her younger gardener (Rock Hudson) and her town turns on her. Technicolor heartbreak.

br.note: A Technicolor witch whose lovers keep dying
Todd Haynes' homage to Sirk

core.b: A girl's lie destroys her sister's love affair (Keira Knightley, James McAvoy), from a 1935 country house to Dunkirk.

br.note: Jane Campion's mute bride in colonial New Zealand. On Sight & Sound's list

core.b: Ang Lee: two Wyoming ranch hands (Heath Ledger, Jake Gyllenhaal) and a love that lasts twenty years in secret.

br.note: Ryan Gosling and Michelle Williams, a marriage falling apart

core.b: Todd Haynes: Cate Blanchett and Rooney Mara fall in love in 1950s New York. Restrained, gorgeous, aching. Metacritic's best film of 2015.

br.note: A summer in 1983 Italy, the peach, the father's speech

br.t: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
br.note: A painter and her subject on a Breton island. On Sight & Sound's list

core.b: Wong Kar-wai: two neighbours whose spouses are cheating almost fall in love. Core on World cinema.
Jean Vigo's newlyweds on a canal barge, a feral old sailor and a lot of cats. Dreamy, French, on both Sight & Sound polls.

core.t: Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans
core.b: Murnau: a farmer tempted to drown his wife falls back in love with her over one day in the city. Silent and astonishing.
